entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-7pwq-q9jf-539h: kobako Sandbox Escape: guest eval reaches host RCE via method_missing → public_send (any bound Service)
entry.content:
kobako Sandbox Escape: guest eval reaches host RCE via method_missing → public_send (any bound Service)

Aliases: CVE-2026-55107

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • kobako — fixed in 0.9.1

### Summary A guest mruby script running inside the Kobako sandbox can execute arbitrary Ruby in the host process, fully escaping the sandbox. ### Details A host embeds bound "Service" objects that guest scripts call across the wasm boundary through the transport dispatcher. The dispatcher passed the guest-supplied method name straight to `Object#public_send` on the bound object, with no restriction to the object's own methods: ```ruby target.public_send(method.to_sym, *args, **kwargs, &block) ``` `public_send` can invoke any public method, including Ruby's ambient reflection surface. A guest pivots through the public `send` into otherwise private Kernel methods: a dispatch request with `method = "send"` and `args = [:eval, "<ruby>"]` evaluates to `target.send(:eval, "<ruby>")`, running…

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-18126: Malicious code in zzhelloworld_socktest (RubyGems)
entry.content:
Malicious code in zzhelloworld_socktest (RubyGems)

Affected:

  • zzhelloworld_socktest

--- _-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_ ## Source: amazon-inspector (4344ab16d08a7e38ea2f32b406453f86d792c0fa17103125ad84ffd0e39c187f) On `require "zzhelloworld_socktest"`, the library's top-level module body opens a TCP connection to the hardcoded remote endpoint 66.78.40.218:32768, reopens STDIN, STDOUT, and STDERR onto that socket, and execs `/bin/sh -i`. Loading the gem gives the operator of that remote host an interactive shell on the installing machine, with no authentication and full process privileges. The gem's stated purpose is a trivial test library, which does not match a remote-shell capability. The destination is a bare IPv4 address unrelated to any declared publisher infrastructure.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6wmf-3r64-vcwv: Crass : Large numeric exponents cause CPU and memory denial of service
entry.content:
Crass : Large numeric exponents cause CPU and memory denial of service

Aliases: CVE-2026-61845

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H

Affected:

  • crass — fixed in 1.0.7

### Impact Crass converts CSS scientific notation number values with unbounded exponentiation before it clamps the result to `Float::MAX`. Applications that use Crass to parse attacker-controlled CSS strings can be forced to spend disproportionate CPU and memory parsing a tiny input, possibly resulting in a crash. ### Patches This is fixed in Crass 1.0.7. ### Related - https://github.com/rubysec/ruby-advisory-db/blob/master/gems/crass/GHSA-6wmf-3r64-vcwv.yml
